guide.summary: OAuth app, standard scopes, own customers (approval path unconfirmed); Extra scopes available only on request (approval path unconfirmed); Public listing in Box Integrations (approval path unconfirmed). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Box (OAUTH2). Box MCP is a separate toolkit that needs your own OAuth app.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio's managed app works. For production you will usually want your own app so users see your brand, and for scopes, dedicated quota and polling.
reasons: Show your app name instead of 'Composio wants to access your account'
Managed app default scopes may not cover what you need
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own gets a dedicated quota
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval
Box MCP toolkit requires your own OAuth app

prerequisites.title: Box developer account
prerequisites.detail: A free developer account gives access to the Developer Console, where OAuth 2.0 apps are created.

prerequisites.title: Enterprise account for extra scopes
prerequisites.detail: Requesting extra scopes needs an enterprise account tier, and free trial accounts cannot request them.

prerequisites.title: Publicly reachable callback URL
prerequisites.detail: To publish for all Box customers, the callback URL must be publicly accessible on the internet.

steps.title: Create Box developer account and log in
steps.detail: Sign up for a free developer account or use your Box enterprise account.
steps.done_when: You can open the Developer Console.

steps.title: Create a User app with OAuth 2.0
steps.detail: In the Developer Console choose New App, select User as the app type, then Create. The type cannot be changed to Server later.
steps.done_when: The app exists with OAuth 2.0 authentication.

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list
steps.detail: Prepare the smallest scope list the agent needs, for example root_readonly or root_readwrite.
steps.done_when: A scope list with a reason per scope is ready.

steps.title: Get Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Set redirect URI and scopes in Box
steps.detail: On the Configuration tab, add the redirect URI (HTTPS, exact match) and select the Application Scopes.
steps.done_when: Both are saved in the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret
steps.detail: Open App Details on the Configuration tab and copy the Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the Box auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and is ready for connected accounts.

steps.title: Request extra scopes from Box support
steps.detail: Contact Box support with a use-case justification for each extra scope. An agent can draft the text.

steps.title: Wait for Box scope decision
steps.detail: Box support reviews each request individually.
steps.done_when: The scope is provisioned or refused.

steps.title: Prepare and submit Box Integrations listing
steps.detail: Follow the Box Integrations checklist and the Developer Console submission flow.

steps.title: Wait for Box partner review
steps.detail: Box reviews the integration. Duration is not documented.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: New OAuth 2.0 apps need exact URI matches. With several URIs configured, omitting redirect_uri gives a redirect_uri_missing error.

traps.title: App type cannot be changed later
traps.detail: An OAuth 2.0 app cannot become a Server app or the reverse. Creating the wrong type means starting over.

traps.title: Token only reaches the user's own files
traps.detail: The OAuth token is tied to the authorizing user, so the app only sees files that user can access.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding
traps.detail: Users see 'Composio wants to access your account' with the managed app, so use your own app in production.

traps.title: Enterprise API allocation
traps.detail: Calls from custom apps count toward the customer's monthly API allocation, and Box may rate-limit tools exceeding it.

blockers.what_it_means: Multiple redirect URIs are configured and the authorization URL has no redirect_uri parameter.
blockers.what_to_do: Include a redirect_uri that exactly matches one configured URI.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the authorization URL and compare it to the configured URIs.

blockers.symptom: Extra scope request is refused or unavailable
blockers.what_it_means: Box approves extra scopes only when the use case requires them, and free trial accounts cannot request them.
blockers.what_to_do: Use an enterprise tier account and write a clear use-case justification.

open_questions: How long does Box partner review for Integrations listing take, and what does it check? Ask Box developer support or read the Box Integrations checklist.
Does Box require its own review for a standard OAuth app used by many outside customers? Ask Box developer support; the pages found show none.
Do customer admins need to authorize a User OAuth app in the Admin Console? Check with a test enterprise account or ask Box support.
How long do Box support scope requests take? Ask Box support.
Does the managed Composio app limit Box scopes? Check the Box toolkit page in Composio.
Not found: what each review or verification checks and what the developer must submit. Checked box.com, box.com.
